scenario: 你想把「先探索再动手」变成一个能当场照着用的工具，而不是靠临场发挥。
scenario_en: You want to turn 'explore before you build' into a tool you can follow on the spot, not improvise.
q: 这套澄清问题 playbook 由什么构成，目标是什么？
q_en: What does the clarifying-questions playbook consist of, and what's its goal?
why: playbook = 五类澄清问题框架 + 十个领域的问题库。目标是在 5–8 分钟内达成需求清晰，把剩下 35+ 分钟留给架构、特征、模型、评估。它把「多探索」落成可执行的清单，避免开局乱问。
why_en: The playbook is a five-category question framework plus a ten-domain question bank, aiming to reach requirement clarity in 5-8 minutes so 35+ minutes remain for architecture, features, model, and evaluation.
options: 一套固定的最优架构模板，任何题目都不必澄清直接套用
五类问题框架 + 十领域问题库，5–8 分钟收敛需求
一份必背的模型清单，按题型对号入座直接选模型
一套评估指标公式集，用于面试收尾时给方案打分
options_en: A fixed set of optimal architecture templates you apply to any problem without clarifying.
A five-category question framework plus a ten-domain question bank that converges requirements in 5-8 minutes.
A must-memorize list of models you slot in by problem type.
A set of evaluation-metric formulas for scoring your design at the end.
optionExplanations: 固定架构模板正是锚定的温床，playbook 反其道而行——先问清需求再定架构。
对；框架保证不漏维度、问题库保证不同领域都有高命中问题，5–8 分钟收敛需求。
背模型清单不解决「该解哪个问题」，playbook 关注的是澄清而非选型。
评估公式是后续产物，playbook 的重心在开局的需求澄清。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed architecture templates are a breeding ground for anchoring; the playbook does the opposite — clarify needs, then choose.
Correct — the framework prevents missing a dimension and the bank ensures a high-hit question per domain, converging needs in 5-8 minutes.
Memorizing a model list doesn't answer which problem to solve; the playbook is about clarification, not model selection.
Evaluation formulas are a downstream product; the playbook focuses on up-front requirement clarification.

scenario: 每个澄清问题都应落进五个「镜头」之一；漏掉某个镜头就留下一个日后要付昂贵中途返工代价的盲点。
scenario_en: Every clarifying question should fall into one of five 'lenses'; skipping a lens leaves a blind spot that later forces a costly mid-interview pivot.
q: 澄清问题的五个类别（镜头）有哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are the five categories (lenses) of clarifying questions? (multiple)
why: 五镜头：业务目标、规模与约束、数据可得性、延迟/精度/成本权衡、干系人情境。每个镜头对应一类会改写下游设计的信息，缺任一个都会在后面爆雷。「用什么编程语言」不是镜头之一。
why_en: The five lenses are business objective, scale and constraints, data availability, latency/accuracy/cost trade-offs, and stakeholder context; each covers information that reshapes the downstream design.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Q["模糊命题"] --> L1["业务目标"]
  Q --> L2["规模与约束"]
  Q --> L3["数据可得性"]
  Q --> L4["延迟/精度/成本"]
  Q --> L5["干系人情境"]
  L1 & L2 & L3 & L4 & L5 --> D["精确的需求集"]
options: 业务目标：成功到底是收入、参与度、安全还是混合
规模与约束：QPS、数据量、地理分布、基础设施上限
干系人情境：输出给谁用（终端用户/内部审核/监管），决定可解释与合规
编程语言选型：用 Python 还是 Go 写服务
options_en: Business objective: whether success is revenue, engagement, safety, or a blend.
Scale and constraints: QPS, data volume, geo distribution, infra limits.
Stakeholder context: who consumes the output (end users / internal review / regulators), driving explainability and compliance.
Programming language choice: whether to write the service in Python or Go.
optionExplanations: 对；业务目标塑造损失函数、离线指标和线上 KPI，是五镜头之首。
对；规模与约束决定单次打分还是多阶段召回-排序，早问能剪掉不可行架构。
对；干系人决定是否需要可解释/合规阶段，是最常被漏掉的镜头。
错；编程语言不改变问题形式化，属于无设计影响的反模式问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — business objective shapes the loss, offline metrics, and online KPIs; it's the first lens.
Correct — scale and constraints decide single-pass vs multi-stage retrieval-ranking, and asking early prunes infeasible architectures.
Correct — stakeholders decide whether you need an explainability/compliance stage; it's the most-skipped lens.
Incorrect — programming language doesn't change the formulation and is a no-design-impact anti-pattern question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求/预测数，衡量吞吐量，是规模镜头的核心数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures throughput and is the core number of the scale lens.

scenario: 五个镜头都要问，但顺序会影响效率：先问对了能尽早剪掉不可行的方案。
scenario_en: You'll ask all five lenses, but order matters: the right sequence prunes infeasible options early.
q: 把五个澄清镜头排成推荐的提问顺序：
q_en: Order the five clarifying lenses in the recommended sequence:
steps: 延迟/精度/成本权衡：定模型复杂度上限
业务目标：先定义什么算成功，它塑造一切
干系人情境：谁用输出、要不要可解释/合规
规模与约束：早问以剪掉不可行架构
数据可得性：标签质量、延迟、冷启动
why: 顺序：业务目标 → 规模与约束 → 数据可得性 → 延迟/精度/成本 → 干系人情境。目标最先，因为它塑造后面一切；规模约束早问，好尽快剪掉不可行的架构，别在无效方案上浪费时间。
why_en: The order is business objective, scale and constraints, data availability, latency/accuracy/cost, then stakeholder context — objective first because it shapes everything, constraints early to prune infeasible architectures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品无历史交互，需靠内容特征或兜底策略，是数据可得性镜头的一项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold-start is when new users or items lack interaction history, needing content features or fallbacks — part of the data-availability lens.

scenario: 命题「首页视频推荐」。用业务目标镜头你问：主目标是最大化观看时长，还是点击率(CTR)？
scenario_en: Prompt: home-page video recommendation. Through the business-objective lens you ask: maximize watch time, or click-through rate (CTR)?
q: 「观看时长 vs CTR」这个回答会怎样改变形式化？
q_en: How does the 'watch time vs CTR' answer change the formulation?
why: 业务目标直接决定损失函数。观看时长是连续值 → 回归；CTR 是点没点的二分类 → 二分类交叉熵。同一个推荐命题，目标不同，模型的学习目标和评估口径就完全不同。
why_en: The business objective sets the loss: watch time is a continuous value (regression), while CTR is click-or-not (binary classification).
whenOtherWins: 如果产品真正在乎的是点击而非停留（如信息流首图点击），CTR 二分类才是对的目标，此时观看时长回归反而偏题。
options: 观看时长做二分类、CTR 做回归，正好反过来
两者都用同一个损失，回答不影响建模
观看时长→回归；CTR→二分类交叉熵，损失不同
无论哪个都只做排序，业务目标不改变任务类型
options_en: Watch time as binary classification and CTR as regression — exactly reversed.
Both use the same loss; the answer doesn't affect modeling.
Watch time goes to regression; CTR to binary cross-entropy, so the loss differs.
Either way you only do ranking; the business objective never changes the task type.
optionExplanations: 说反了：连续的观看时长对应回归，二元的点击对应分类。
回答直接换损失函数，怎么会不影响建模——这正是业务目标镜头的意义。
对；目标是连续量还是二元事件，直接决定回归还是分类，损失和评估随之变。
任务类型恰恰随目标而变；把一切默认成排序会错配损失与指标。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: continuous watch time maps to regression, binary clicks to classification.
The answer directly swaps the loss, so it certainly affects modeling — that's the point of the objective lens.
Correct — whether the target is a continuous quantity or a binary event decides regression vs classification, and the loss/metric follow.
Task type does change with the objective; defaulting everything to ranking misaligns loss and metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击数除以曝光数，衡量点击倾向；作为目标时对应二分类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is clicks divided by impressions, measuring propensity to click; as a target it maps to binary classification.

tradeoff: 回归（观看时长）vs 二分类（CTR）：目标是连续值还是点没点，直接换掉损失函数。

scenario: 首页视频推荐，规模镜头你问：每个请求要打分多少候选视频？（YouTube 级：20 亿+ 用户、上亿视频）
scenario_en: For home-page video rec, through the scale lens you ask: how many candidate videos are scored per request? (YouTube scale: 2B+ users, 100M+ videos.)
q: 候选规模的答案，如何决定「单次打分 vs 多阶段召回-排序」？
q_en: How does the candidate-set size decide 'single-pass scoring vs multi-stage retrieval-ranking'?
why: 候选规模决定架构形态。若每请求只需在几百个候选里排序，单次打分就够；若要从上亿视频里选，就必须多阶段——先轻量 retrieval 把上亿缩到几百，再重模型 ranking。10K 请求/天和 10M 请求/秒是两个不同宇宙。
why_en: Candidate-set size decides the architecture: a few hundred candidates allow single-pass scoring, but 100M+ videos force multi-stage retrieval to shrink the pool before ranking.
whenOtherWins: 如果候选集本就很小（如已按频道预筛到几十个），单次打分更简单，多阶段召回反而是过度设计。
options: 候选越多越该单次打分，一次算完最省事、也最省机器
候选规模只影响服务器数量，不改变架构形态
上亿候选→多阶段召回+排序；几百→单次打分
无论规模都用多阶段，这是唯一正确的推荐架构
options_en: The more candidates, the more you should single-pass score — one shot is simplest and cheapest.
Candidate-set size only affects server count, not the shape of the architecture.
100M+ candidates go multi-stage (retrieval then ranking); a few hundred allow single-pass scoring.
Use multi-stage regardless of scale — it is the only correct recommendation architecture.
optionExplanations: 说反了：候选越多越不可能逐个重打分，反而必须先召回缩小。
规模先决定用不用得起单次重打分，再谈扩容，不只是服务器数。
对；上亿候选逼你先 retrieval 缩小再 ranking，这是规模镜头的核心决策。
小候选集上多阶段是过度设计；架构应随规模选，不是一刀切。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: more candidates make per-item heavy scoring less feasible, forcing retrieval to shrink first.
Scale first decides whether single-pass heavy scoring is affordable, before server count.
Correct — 100M+ candidates force retrieval-then-ranking; that's the scale lens's core decision.
Multi-stage on a small candidate set is over-engineering; architecture should follow scale, not be one-size-fits-all.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["上亿候选视频"] --> R["轻量 retrieval
缩到几百"] R --> K["重模型 ranking
精排"] K --> O["最终推荐列表"]
tradeoff: 单次打分 vs 多阶段召回-排序：几百候选省一层复杂度，上亿候选只能牺牲少量召回率换算力。

scenario: 首页视频推荐，数据镜头你问：有显式评分(星级)，还是只有隐式信号（点击、停留）？
scenario_en: For home-page video rec, through the data lens you ask: are there explicit ratings (stars), or only implicit signals (clicks, dwell)?
q: 「显式评分 vs 只有隐式信号」为什么值得先问清？
q_en: Why is 'explicit ratings vs implicit signals only' worth clarifying first?
why: 这决定标签怎么定义和怎么去噪。显式评分是干净直接的监督；只有隐式信号时，点击/停留是有偏、带噪的代理标签（误点、标题党），要专门处理噪声和位置偏差。没问清就默认，标签口径可能从一开始就错。
why_en: It decides how labels are defined and denoised: explicit ratings are clean supervision, while implicit signals like clicks are biased, noisy proxies needing special noise and bias handling.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品确实有大量可信显式评分，就不必围绕隐式信号去搭复杂的去噪/去偏，直接用干净标签更省事。
options: 问不问都行，点击信号天然干净，可以直接当标签用
它决定标签定义与去噪：隐式信号有偏带噪
它只影响日志的存储格式，建模照旧不受影响
显式评分总是更差，任何场景都该一律改用隐式信号
options_en: It doesn't matter — click signals are inherently clean and usable directly as labels.
It decides label definition and denoising: implicit signals are biased and noisy.
It only affects the log storage format; modeling is unaffected.
Explicit ratings are always worse; you should always switch to implicit signals.
optionExplanations: 点击并不干净：有标题党、误点、位置偏差，直接当标签会学偏。
对；标签是显式还是隐式，直接决定要不要做去噪/去偏，是数据镜头的关键。
它先决定标签口径与噪声处理，远不止存储格式。
显式评分往往更干净，只是量少；不该一律弃用。
optionExplanations_en: Clicks aren't clean: clickbait, misclicks, and position bias mean using them raw teaches the wrong thing.
Correct — explicit vs implicit labels directly decides whether you need denoising/debiasing; that's the data lens's crux.
It first decides label definition and noise handling, far beyond storage format.
Explicit ratings are often cleaner, just sparser; you shouldn't discard them wholesale.
tradeoff: 显式评分 vs 隐式信号：标签干净但稀少，vs 量大但有偏、要做去噪与位置纠偏。

scenario: 首页视频推荐，延迟镜头你问：首页 SLA 大概是 200ms 吗？
scenario_en: For home-page video rec, through the latency lens you ask: is the homepage SLA around 200ms?
q: 确认 ~200ms 首页 SLA 后，它约束掉了什么？
q_en: Once you confirm a ~200ms homepage SLA, what does it rule out?
why: ~200ms 的首页 SLA 直接约束模型复杂度：来不及给每个候选跑一个大 transformer。它把方案推向轻量打分+预计算，或把重模型只留给少量候选的精排阶段。宽松预算才容得下集成模型。
why_en: A ~200ms homepage SLA constrains complexity — you can't run a large transformer per candidate — pushing you to lightweight scoring or reserving heavy models for a small re-ranking stage.
whenOtherWins: 如果是可异步、离线预计算的推荐（如每日推送而非首屏实时），延迟宽松，就能负担更重的集成模型。
options: 200ms 很宽松，可以给每个候选都跑一个大 transformer
它只影响缓存策略，和模型大小、候选数都无关
它约束模型复杂度：逼向轻量打分+预计算
它意味着必须换最大的模型，才能抢在 200ms 内算完
options_en: 200ms is generous — you can run a large transformer per candidate.
It only affects caching strategy, unrelated to model size or candidate count.
It constrains model complexity, pushing you toward lightweight scoring plus precompute.
It means you must switch to the largest model to finish inside 200ms.
optionExplanations: 200ms 对上亿候选逐个跑大模型远不够宽松，反而是硬约束。
它首先约束模型能多复杂，不只是缓存。
对；SLA 先砍掉重模型逐候选推理，逼你把重活挪到少量精排或离线预计算。
说反了：越大的模型越进不了 200ms，SLA 要的是更轻。
optionExplanations_en: 200ms is far from generous for a large model per candidate over 100M+; it's a hard constraint.
It first constrains how complex the model can be, not just caching.
Correct — the SLA cuts per-candidate heavy inference, pushing heavy work to a small shortlist or offline precompute.
Backwards: bigger models are less able to fit 200ms; the SLA demands lighter ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外承诺的服务指标，这里是首页端到端响应延迟上限 ~200ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed service target, here the homepage end-to-end latency ceiling of ~200ms.

tradeoff: 轻量打分+预计算 vs 重模型精排：延迟预算 vs 模型表达力。

scenario: 首页视频推荐，干系人镜头你问：信任与安全(Trust & Safety)团队对「压制某视频」需不需要可解释性？
scenario_en: For home-page video rec, through the stakeholder lens you ask: does Trust & Safety need explainability for suppressing a video?
q: 若 T&S 需要可解释的压制理由，架构要加什么？
q_en: If Trust & Safety needs an explainable suppression reason, what must the architecture add?
why: 干系人若是内部审核/监管，就需要能解释「为什么压这条」。这会加一个可解释层或独立的策略过滤(policy-filter)阶段——把可解释的规则/信号从黑箱排序里拆出来，供审核追溯。忽视它会让整套架构后期被合规否决。
why_en: If the consumer is internal review or regulators, you must explain why a video was suppressed, adding an interpretability layer or a separate policy-filter stage.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出只面向终端用户、没有压制/合规审查需求，就不必加策略过滤阶段，保持排序管线简单即可。
options: 加可解释层/独立策略过滤，让压制可追溯
不用改，排序模型的黑箱分数已足够解释压制理由
换成更大的黑箱模型，用精度提升代替解释能力
只需在日志里多存几个字段，架构完全不用动
options_en: Add an interpretability layer or a separate policy-filter stage so suppression is auditable.
No change — the ranking model's black-box score already explains suppression.
Swap in a larger black-box model and let accuracy substitute for explainability.
Just store a few more log fields; the architecture stays untouched.
optionExplanations: 对；可解释需求要求把策略/信号单独成阶段，供 T&S 追溯，是架构级改动。
黑箱分数解释不了「为什么压这条」，满足不了审核和合规。
更大的黑箱只会更难解释，与可解释需求背道而驰。
多存字段不等于可解释；需要的是可追溯的策略阶段，是结构性改动。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — explainability requires a separate policy/signal stage that T&S can trace, an architecture-level change.
A black-box score can't explain why a specific video was suppressed and fails audit and compliance.
A bigger black box is even harder to explain, opposite to the explainability need.
Logging more fields isn't explainability; you need a traceable policy stage, a structural change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责内容合规、压制违规内容的团队，常需要可解释、可追溯的决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Trust & Safety is the team handling content compliance and suppression, often needing explainable, auditable decisions.

termDefinitions.term: policy-filter stage / 策略过滤阶段
termDefinitions.meaning: 排序之外独立的一层，用可解释规则/信号决定是否压制或过滤内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A policy-filter stage is a layer separate from ranking that applies explainable rules/signals to suppress or filter content.

tradeoff: 黑箱排序 vs 可解释策略过滤：排序效果 vs 可审计性，拆出规则层会损失一点排序收益。

scenario: 时间紧，你倾向于跳过干系人相关的澄清问题，直接进架构。
scenario_en: Short on time, you're tempted to skip stakeholder-related clarifying questions and jump to architecture.
q: 为什么「跳过干系人问题」是最危险的省略？
q_en: Why is skipping stakeholder questions the most dangerous omission?
why: 干系人问题是最常被漏的一类，代价却最大：监管/可解释要求往往到后期才浮现，而它们可能直接推翻整套架构（如必须可解释就不能用你选的黑箱大模型）。晚发现=昂贵的推倒重来。
why_en: Stakeholder questions are the most commonly skipped, yet regulatory/explainability requirements surface late and can invalidate the entire architecture, forcing an expensive rebuild.
options: 干系人问题最不重要，时间紧时跳过基本没风险
它最常被漏，监管/可解释要求晚发现会推翻架构
跳过它只影响文档完整度，不会改变任何设计决策
干系人问题只在健康医疗类题目里才有必要问
options_en: Stakeholder questions matter least, so skipping them when time is tight is basically risk-free.
It's the most-skipped category, and late-surfacing regulatory or explainability requirements can invalidate the architecture.
Skipping it only affects documentation completeness, never a design decision.
Stakeholder questions are only worth asking on health-tech problems.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反：它最常被漏，且漏掉的代价可能是整套架构作废。
对；合规/可解释是架构级约束，晚问就晚发现，代价是中途推倒重来。
它不是文档问题：一条合规要求能让你选的黑箱模型直接不可用。
监管/可解释在金融、内容审核、广告等多领域都出现，不限医疗。
optionExplanations_en: Quite the opposite: it's the most-skipped, and skipping it can void the whole architecture.
Correct — compliance/explainability are architecture-level constraints; asking late means finding out late, at the cost of a rebuild.
It's not a documentation issue: one compliance rule can make your chosen black-box model unusable.
Regulatory/explainability appears across finance, moderation, ads, and more — not just health-tech.

scenario: 你担心离线指标涨了、线上业务却没动——即所谓 offline-to-online gap。
scenario_en: You worry the offline metric improves while online business doesn't move — the so-called offline-to-online gap.
q: 业务目标镜头里，怎样收窄「离线到线上」的差距？
q_en: Within the business-objective lens, how do you close the offline-to-online gap?
why: 把离线指标和线上 KPI 对齐：让离线指标（如 NDCG、AUC）尽量代理你真正在乎的线上 KPI（转化、观看时长）。对齐了，离线涨才对应线上赚；不对齐就会出现离线到线上的鸿沟——离线更好、线上无感甚至更差。
why_en: Align the offline metric with the online KPI so the offline proxy (e.g. NDCG, AUC) tracks the KPI you actually care about, making an offline gain correspond to an online win.
options: 尽量选和业务无关但数值好看的离线指标来汇报
把离线指标与线上 KPI 对齐，让它代理业务结果
彻底放弃离线指标，只看线上 A/B 的最终结果
离线线上本就无法对齐，随便选个离线指标即可
options_en: Pick offline metrics that look good numerically but have nothing to do with the business.
Align the offline metric with the online KPI so it proxies the business outcome.
Abandon offline metrics entirely and only look at the final online A/B result.
Offline and online can never align, so any offline metric will do.
optionExplanations: 好看但无关的离线指标正是鸿沟之源：离线涨、线上不动。
对；离线指标是线上 KPI 的代理，代理得越准，离线迭代越能预示线上收益。
全弃离线会失去快速迭代能力；正解是让离线对齐线上，而非二选一。
对齐是可做的工程目标，不是随缘——放弃对齐就等于放任鸿沟。
optionExplanations_en: Good-looking but unrelated offline metrics are the source of the gap: offline rises, online doesn't move.
Correct — the offline metric proxies the online KPI, and the better the proxy, the more offline iteration predicts online gains.
Abandoning offline loses fast iteration; the fix is aligning offline to online, not either/or.
Alignment is an achievable engineering goal, not luck; giving up on it lets the gap run wild.

termDefinitions.term: offline-to-online gap / 离线到线上鸿沟
termDefinitions.meaning: 离线指标提升却不带来线上 KPI 改善的现象，源于离线指标未对齐真实业务目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The offline-to-online gap is when offline metric gains don't translate to online KPI improvements, from a misaligned offline metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序质量的离线指标，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a ranking-quality offline metric that rewards relevant results placed higher.

scenario: 广告(Ads)题的高命中澄清问题：计费是按点击(CPC)还是按千次曝光(CPM)？
scenario_en: High-hit clarifying question for Ads: is billing per click (CPC) or per thousand impressions (CPM)?
q: CPC 计费和 CPM 计费，会把预测目标推向哪里？
q_en: How do CPC vs CPM billing steer the prediction target?
why: 计费模式直接换损失。CPC 按点击收费 → 要预测点击概率（pCTR）；CPM 按曝光收费 → 目标转向曝光价值/展示优化，不再以点击为核心标签。没问计费就默认 pCTR，可能优化了一个和收入错位的目标。
why_en: The billing model swaps the loss: CPC bills per click, so you predict click probability, while CPM bills per impression, shifting the target to impression value rather than clicks.
tradeoff: CPC(预测点击概率 pCTR) vs CPM(优化曝光价值，不以点击为核心标签)
options: CPC 和 CPM 只是报价单位，不影响建模目标与标签
CPC → 预测曝光价值；CPM → 预测点击概率，正好相反
CPC→预测 pCTR；CPM→转向曝光价值/展示优化
两种计费都只需预测转化率，与点击、曝光都无关
options_en: CPC and CPM are just pricing units; they affect neither the modeling target nor the label.
CPC predicts impression value; CPM predicts click probability — the reverse.
CPC predicts pCTR; CPM shifts to impression value and display optimization.
Both billing models only need conversion-rate prediction, unrelated to clicks or impressions.
optionExplanations: 计费单位恰恰决定优化目标：按什么收费就该优化什么。
说反了：按点击收费(CPC)对应点击概率，按曝光收费(CPM)对应曝光价值。
对；CPC 优化 pCTR、CPM 优化曝光价值，标签和损失随计费而变。
转化率是更下游的目标；CPC/CPM 的核心分野在点击 vs 曝光。
optionExplanations_en: The billing unit is exactly what sets the optimization target: optimize what you're paid for.
Backwards: billing per click (CPC) maps to click probability, per impression (CPM) to impression value.
Correct — CPC optimizes pCTR, CPM optimizes impression value; label and loss follow the billing model.
Conversion rate is a more downstream target; the CPC/CPM split is fundamentally clicks vs impressions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按点击计费的广告模式，广告主每次被点击才付费，模型核心是预测点击概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CPC (Cost Per Click) bills advertisers per click, so the model's core is predicting click probability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每千次曝光计费的广告模式，优化目标转向曝光价值而非点击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CPM (Cost Per Mille) bills per thousand impressions, shifting the optimization target to impression value rather than clicks.

scenario: 命题「为一家支付公司做欺诈检测」。你要问一个最能改写设计的澄清问题。
scenario_en: Prompt: fraud detection for a payments company. You must ask the one clarifying question that most reshapes the design.
q: 对支付欺诈，最关键的澄清问题是什么？为什么？
q_en: What's the most critical clarifying question for payment fraud, and why?
why: 最关键的是「交易发生到欺诈被确认之间的标签延迟」。chargeback 可能几小时、几天甚至几个月才到，延迟长就意味着训练时大量样本还没盖棺，必须按延迟反馈来设计（等待窗、代理标签、样本重加权），这是整个方案的分水岭。
why_en: The most critical is the label delay between a transaction and confirmed fraud, because chargebacks can take hours, days, or months, forcing delayed-feedback training design.
whenOtherWins: 如果场景里标签几乎实时（如即时风控规则立即打标），延迟反馈那套就不必要，可直接用近实时监督训练。
options: 该用哪种梯度提升库来训模型（XGBoost 还是 LightGBM）
交易到欺诈确认之间的标签延迟有多久
服务器要部署在哪个云厂商的哪个区域
欺诈交易的平均金额和中位金额分别是多少
options_en: Which gradient-boosting library to train with (XGBoost or LightGBM).
How long the label delay is between a transaction and confirmed fraud.
Which cloud vendor and region the servers should be deployed in.
What the average and median dollar amounts of fraudulent transactions are.
optionExplanations: 选哪个库是实现细节，改变不了问题形式化，属于低影响问题。
对；标签延迟决定训练时有多少确定标签，是欺诈问题最能分叉设计的澄清点。
云区域是部署细节，不改变欺诈问题的建模。
平均金额是背景数据，不像标签延迟那样重塑训练方式。
optionExplanations_en: Which library is an implementation detail that doesn't change the formulation — a low-impact question.
Correct — label delay decides how many confirmed labels you have at training time, the highest-forking clarification for fraud.
Cloud region is a deployment detail that doesn't change the fraud modeling.
Average amount is background data, unlike label delay it doesn't reshape how you train.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从预测发生到真值标签确定之间的时间；欺诈里因 chargeback 常达数月。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label delay is the time from prediction to when the ground-truth label is confirmed; in fraud it's often months due to chargebacks.

termDefinitions.term: delayed-feedback training / 延迟反馈训练
termDefinitions.meaning: 针对标签晚到设计的训练方式，处理暂时无标签或标签会翻转的样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed-feedback training is designed for late-arriving labels, handling temporarily unlabeled or later-flipping samples.

tradeoff: 等标签盖棺再训 vs 用代理标签早训：标签准确 vs 数据新鲜。

scenario: 内容审核题，你问：对误报(FP)和漏报(FN)各自的容忍度如何？（言论自由 vs 监管压力）
scenario_en: Content moderation: you ask about tolerance for false positives (FP) vs false negatives (FN) — free speech vs regulatory pressure.
q: FP/FN 容忍度这个回答，会怎样牵动审核策略？
q_en: How does the FP/FN-tolerance answer steer the moderation strategy?
why: 两类错误代价方向相反：激进删除降低漏报但推高误报，误伤合法内容→用户反弹、言论自由争议；宽松审核降低误报但推高漏报→违规内容漏网、招监管处罚。容忍度决定阈值和损失里 FP/FN 的相对权重。
why_en: The two errors trade off oppositely: aggressive removal cuts false negatives but raises false positives (user backlash), while under-moderation cuts false positives but raises false negatives (regulatory risk).
options: 两类错误一样糟，阈值取居中就行，不必分开权衡
激进删除降 FN 升 FP，宽松审核反过来，容忍度定阈值
只要提高整体准确率，FP 和 FN 会一起下降，无需权衡
FP/FN 容忍度只影响文档措辞，不会改变模型阈值
options_en: Both errors are equally bad, so a middle threshold works and no separate weighting is needed.
Aggressive removal cuts FN but raises FP; lenient moderation does the reverse, and tolerance sets the threshold.
Just raise overall accuracy and both FP and FN drop together, so no trade-off is needed.
FP/FN tolerance only affects documentation wording, never the model threshold.
optionExplanations: 两类错误代价通常不对称，居中阈值等于回避了这道题的核心权衡。
对；容忍度方向决定你把阈值往哪调、损失里 FP/FN 谁权重更大。
FP 和 FN 常此消彼长，靠单纯提准确率两头兼得并不现实。
它直接改阈值和损失权重，不是措辞问题。
optionExplanations_en: The two errors usually have asymmetric costs; a middle threshold dodges this problem's core trade-off.
Correct — the tolerance direction decides which way to move the threshold and which of FP/FN gets more weight in the loss.
FP and FN usually trade off; getting both via raw accuracy gains is unrealistic.
It directly changes the threshold and loss weighting, not just wording.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把合法内容判为违规、错误删除，造成用户反弹与言论自由争议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) flags legitimate content as violating, causing wrongful removal, backlash, and free-speech disputes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把违规内容判为合法、放行，导致有害内容漏网、招致监管处罚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) passes violating content as legitimate, letting harmful content through and inviting regulatory penalties.

scenario: 推荐系统题，你问冷启动比例：主要是新用户多，还是新物品多？
scenario_en: Recommendation: you ask the cold-start ratio — mostly new users, or mostly new items?
q: 冷启动比例的答案，如何决定召回策略？
q_en: How does the cold-start ratio decide the retrieval strategy?
why: 冷启动严重时，纯协同过滤(CF)对无历史的新用户/新物品失效。答案指向要不要上内容兜底：新物品多 → 靠内容特征给它冷启动打分；老用户老物品稳定 → 协同过滤就够。比例决定你偏内容还是偏协同。
why_en: Severe cold-start breaks pure collaborative filtering for history-less new users/items, so the answer decides whether you add a content-based fallback rather than relying on collaborative filtering.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户和物品都稳定、几乎没有新增，纯协同过滤足矣，不必额外搭内容兜底管线。
options: 冷启动比例不影响召回，协同过滤对新用户同样有效
冷启动严重→需内容兜底；稳定→纯协同过滤即可
冷启动越严重越该纯协同过滤，内容特征帮不上忙
只要多收集一段时间点击数据，冷启动会自动消失
options_en: The cold-start ratio doesn't affect retrieval; collaborative filtering works for new users too.
Severe cold-start needs a content-based fallback; a stable base allows pure collaborative filtering.
The more severe the cold-start, the more you should use pure collaborative filtering; content features do not help.
Just collect click data for a while longer and cold-start disappears on its own.
optionExplanations: 协同过滤对无交互历史的新项是空的，冷启动严重时必然失效。
对；比例高就得靠内容特征兜底，比例低协同过滤够用，这是推荐领域的关键分叉。
说反了：冷启动严重恰恰是协同过滤的软肋，得靠内容特征补。
新项一开始就没数据，不是「多收集」能立即解决的，冷启动是结构性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Collaborative filtering is empty for new items with no interaction history and fails under severe cold-start.
Correct — a high ratio needs content-based fallback, a low one allows collaborative filtering; that's recommendation's key fork.
Backwards: severe cold-start is exactly collaborative filtering's weak spot, needing content features.
New items have no data from the start; 'collect more' can't fix it immediately — cold-start is structural.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠用户-物品交互历史找相似模式来推荐，对无历史的新用户/新物品失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering (CF) recommends by finding patterns in user-item interaction history, failing for history-less new users/items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用物品自身内容特征（文本、图片、类别）打分，不依赖交互历史，适合冷启动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-based recommendation scores items by their own content features (text, images, category) without interaction history, suiting cold-start.

tradeoff: 内容特征兜底 vs 纯协同过滤：新用户新物品的覆盖 vs 老用户老物品上的精度。

scenario: 搜索排序题，你问：排序目标是相关性、收入，还是二者混合？
scenario_en: Search ranking: you ask whether the objective is relevance, revenue, or a blend.
q: 「相关性 vs 收入 vs 混合」为什么必须先问清？
q_en: Why must you clarify 'relevance vs revenue vs blend' first?
why: 这决定用什么特征、什么损失。纯相关性 → 用查询-文档匹配特征、排序损失优化相关；含收入 → 要引入竞价/利润特征、把收入并入目标（可能多目标加权）。目标混合方式不同，特征工程和损失完全不同。
why_en: It decides features and loss: pure relevance uses query-document match features and a ranking loss, while a revenue blend adds bid/margin features and folds revenue into the objective.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确只优化相关性（如站内文档检索，无广告变现），就不必引入收入特征，纯相关性排序更简单。
options: 无所谓，搜索排序在任何业务里都只优化相关性
它决定特征与损失：相关性用匹配特征，收入要加竞价特征
它只影响结果页 UI 的展示顺序，模型完全不用动
混合目标一定更好，任何搜索都该同时塞进收入信号
options_en: It doesn't matter — search ranking only ever optimizes relevance.
It decides features and loss: relevance uses match features, revenue adds bid features.
It only affects the result-page UI order; the model stays untouched.
A blended objective is always better; every search should fold in a revenue signal.
optionExplanations: 很多搜索要变现，默认只优化相关性会漏掉收入这条目标线。
对；目标是纯相关还是含收入，直接换特征集和损失结构，是搜索题的分叉点。
它改的是模型的目标与特征，不只是展示顺序。
强行塞收入会牺牲相关性、伤长期体验；是否混合要看业务，不是一律更好。
optionExplanations_en: Many searches monetize, so defaulting to relevance-only misses the revenue objective.
Correct — pure relevance vs revenue-blended directly swaps the feature set and loss structure, search ranking's key fork.
It changes the model's objective and features, not just display order.
Forcing in revenue can sacrifice relevance and long-term experience; whether to blend depends on the business, not always better.
tradeoff: 相关性 vs 收入：用户满意 vs 变现，混合目标还要额外定一个权重。

scenario: 生成式 AI 题（如聊天助手），你问：需要哪些安全与幻觉防护(guardrails)？
scenario_en: Generative AI (e.g. a chat assistant): you ask what safety and hallucination guardrails are required.
q: 确认需要安全/防幻觉后，架构上要补什么？
q_en: Once safety/anti-hallucination is required, what must the architecture add?
why: 生成式的高命中问题是防护要求。要么加一个安全分类器过滤有害输出，要么用 RAG 把回答锚定到可检索的真实文档来抑制幻觉，要么在高风险场景加人类在环(HITL)审核。防护需求决定这几个组件加不加，是架构级取舍。
why_en: The high-hit generative question is guardrail requirements: add a safety classifier to filter harmful output, RAG grounding to curb hallucination, or a human-in-the-loop reviewer for high-risk cases.
whenOtherWins: 如果是低风险、内部工具且输出不外发，防护可以从简，不必上完整安全分类器+RAG+HITL 全套。
options: 只要把模型调大，幻觉和安全问题自然消失，不用加组件
视需求加安全分类器、RAG 锚定文档或人类在环
把温度调到 0 就能彻底杜绝幻觉，无需其他防护
安全防护只是加免责声明文案，不影响架构
options_en: Just make the model bigger and hallucination/safety issues vanish, no components needed.
As needed, add a safety classifier, RAG grounding, or a human in the loop.
Set temperature to 0 to eliminate hallucination entirely, no other guardrails needed.
Safety guardrails are just a disclaimer text, not an architecture concern.
optionExplanations: 更大的模型照样幻觉、照样输出有害内容，规模不替代防护组件。
对；安全分类器、RAG 接地、人类在环是三种真实防护手段，按风险选配，属架构级决定。
温度=0 只让输出更确定，并不保证事实正确，压不住幻觉。
防护是真实组件（分类器/检索/审核），不是免责声明文案。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger model still hallucinates and can emit harmful content; scale doesn't replace guardrail components.
Correct — a safety classifier, RAG grounding, and human-in-the-loop are three real guardrails chosen by risk, an architecture-level decision.
Temperature 0 only makes output more deterministic, not factually correct, and doesn't stop hallucination.
Guardrails are real components (classifier/retrieval/review), not a disclaimer text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检索相关真实文档，再让模型基于它们生成，用可核查的证据抑制幻觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves relevant real documents and grounds generation in them to curb hallucination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在高风险输出前后加入人工审核，作为最后一道安全防线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) inserts human review around high-risk outputs as a final safety check.

tradeoff: 加防护组件 vs 直接放行模型输出：安全与可追溯 vs 多一跳的延迟和成本。

scenario: 计算机视觉题，你问分辨率/帧率和是否边缘(edge)推理：目标是手机端 30 fps 实时。
scenario_en: Computer vision: you ask about resolution/frame rate and edge inference — the target is 30 fps real-time on a phone.
q: 「手机端 30 fps 边缘推理」这个约束逼你做什么？
q_en: What does the '30 fps on-device edge inference' constraint force you to do?
why: 30 fps = 每帧只有约 33ms，还要在手机算力和电量内跑完。这逼你用量化、蒸馏把模型压小；云端大模型因往返延迟直接出局。
why_en: 30 fps gives about 33ms per frame on limited phone compute, forcing model compression — quantization and distillation — rather than a large cloud model.
whenOtherWins: 如果推理可以放云端、延迟宽松（如离线批量分析录像），就不必量化/蒸馏，能直接上大模型换精度。
options: 直接调用云端最大的视觉模型，精度优先，延迟和断网都不重要
每帧约 33ms 且受电量限制 → 量化、蒸馏压小模型
把分辨率拉到最高来提精度，帧率会自动跟上
30 fps 很宽松，无需任何模型压缩
options_en: Just call the largest cloud vision model — accuracy first, latency and offline use do not matter.
About 33ms per frame under battery limits forces quantization and distillation to shrink the model.
Crank resolution to the max to boost accuracy; frame rate will keep up automatically.
30 fps is generous and needs no model compression.
optionExplanations: 云端大模型有网络往返延迟、且离线时不可用，满足不了端上 30 fps 实时。
对；每帧 33ms + 手机算力上限逼你量化/蒸馏，把模型压到能在边缘实时跑。
拉高分辨率会增加计算、拖慢帧率，和 30 fps 目标相冲。
手机端 30 fps 是硬实时约束，反而最需要压缩，不宽松。
optionExplanations_en: A large cloud model has round-trip latency and fails offline, missing on-device 30 fps real-time.
Correct — 33ms/frame plus phone compute limits force quantization/distillation to fit real-time on the edge.
Raising resolution adds compute and slows frame rate, clashing with the 30 fps target.
On-device 30 fps is a hard real-time constraint that most needs compression, not generous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重从高精度(如 FP32)降到低精度(如 INT8)，减小体积、加速推理，略损精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers model weights from high precision (FP32) to low (INT8), shrinking size and speeding inference at slight accuracy cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(teacher)的输出训练小模型(student)，让小模型逼近大模型效果，便于边缘部署。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distillation trains a small student model on a large teacher's outputs so it approximates the teacher, easing edge deployment.

tradeoff: 云端大模型 vs 边缘压缩模型：精度 vs 33ms/帧的实时性和手机电量。

scenario: NLP 题，你问：需要多语言/跨语言迁移吗，还是只做单一语言？
scenario_en: NLP: you ask whether multilingual / cross-lingual transfer is needed, or a single language only.
q: 「要不要多语言」这个回答，牵动哪些设计选择？
q_en: What design choices does the 'multilingual or not' answer drive?
why: 多语言需求牵动分词器、嵌入和模型拓扑：要不要用能覆盖多语言的分词器与共享嵌入，是训一个多语言大模型（共享表示、便于低资源语言迁移）还是每语言各一个（更专精但成本翻倍）。单语言就没这些顾虑。
why_en: Multilingual needs drive tokenizer, embeddings, and topology: a shared multilingual tokenizer/embedding and whether to train one multilingual model versus one per language.
whenOtherWins: 如果只服务单一语言，就用该语言专用分词器和单模型，避免多语言共享带来的容量稀释与折中。
options: 不影响，分词器和嵌入用同一套词表就能覆盖所有语言
牵动分词器/嵌入/拓扑：一个多语言模型 vs 每语言一个
只影响界面 i18n 翻译文案，分词器和模型架构都不用改
推理前用翻译 API 转成单一语言即可，模型完全不用改动
options_en: No effect — sharing one tokenizer/embedding vocabulary naturally covers every language.
It drives tokenizer, embeddings, and topology: one multilingual model vs one per language.
It only affects UI i18n copy; neither the tokenizer nor model architecture changes.
Just translate to a single language with an API before inference; the model needs no change at all.
optionExplanations: 分词器和嵌入的词表通常是按语言训练的，共享一套并不天然覆盖所有语言。
对；多语言需求直接决定分词、嵌入和是单模型还是多模型，是 NLP 题的关键分叉。
它改的是模型的分词器/嵌入/拓扑架构，不只是界面 i18n 文案。
推理前套翻译 API 会丢语义、增延迟，不等于原生多语言建模能力。
optionExplanations_en: Tokenizer and embedding vocabularies are usually trained per language; sharing one vocab doesn't naturally cover every language.
Correct — multilingual needs directly decide tokenizer, embeddings, and single vs multi model, NLP's key fork.
It changes the model's tokenizer/embeddings/architecture, not just UI i18n copy.
A pre-inference translation API loses semantics and adds latency — not the same as native multilingual modeling.
tradeoff: 一个多语言模型 vs 每语言一个：共享表示便于低资源迁移 vs 更专精但成本翻倍。

scenario: 健康医疗题，你问：有没有 HIPAA 等对数据和可解释性的监管约束？
scenario_en: Health-tech: you ask whether there are regulatory constraints like HIPAA on data and explainability.
q: 确认存在 HIPAA/可解释监管后，它主要限制了什么？
q_en: Once HIPAA / explainability regulation is confirmed, what does it mainly constrain?
why: 医疗监管把可解释性设成硬约束：临床决策通常必须能解释，直接排除不可解释的黑箱大模型，倾向可解释模型（或加可解释层）。HIPAA 还限制数据如何存储、脱敏、流转。这类约束是架构级红线，晚发现会全盘作废。
why_en: Health regulation makes explainability a hard constraint that rules out opaque black-box models in favor of interpretable ones, and HIPAA also restricts how data is stored and handled.
whenOtherWins: 如果是非临床、无个人健康信息的场景（如公开医学文献检索），监管约束弱，就不必强制可解释模型。
options: 只限制服务器部署在哪个地理区域，不影响模型选择
把可解释性设成硬约束，排除黑箱大模型
要求必须用最大的深度模型，以保证诊断精度达标
只影响 UI 是否显示免责声明，完全不涉及建模
options_en: It only restricts which geographic region the servers sit in, not model choice.
It makes explainability a hard constraint, ruling out black-box large models.
It requires the largest deep model to guarantee diagnostic accuracy.
It only affects whether the UI shows a disclaimer, with no modeling impact.
optionExplanations: 监管首先约束模型可解释性和数据处理，不只是服务器位置。
对；可解释是硬约束，直接砍掉黑箱模型，还叠加 HIPAA 的数据合规要求。
说反了：越大的黑箱越不可解释，正是监管要排除的。
它改的是模型可选集和数据流转，不是免责声明文案。
optionExplanations_en: Regulation first constrains model explainability and data handling, not just server location.
Correct — explainability is a hard constraint that cuts black-box models, plus HIPAA's data-compliance requirements.
Backwards: bigger black boxes are less explainable, exactly what regulation rules out.
It changes the feasible model set and data flow, not a disclaimer text.

termDefinitions.fullName: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
termDefinitions.meaning: 美国医疗数据隐私与安全法规，约束受保护健康信息的存储、访问与流转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) is the US law governing storage, access, and handling of protected health information.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于博弈论 Shapley 值给每个特征归因贡献的可解释方法，常用于满足可解释监管。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attributes each feature's contribution using game-theoretic Shapley values, common for explainability compliance.

tradeoff: 可解释模型 vs 黑箱大模型：合规可审计 vs 精度上限。

scenario: 双边市场题（如打车、电商平台），你问：要不要同时优化买方满意度和卖方公平？
scenario_en: Marketplace (ride-hailing, e-commerce): you ask whether to optimize both buyer satisfaction and seller fairness.
q: 「双边优化」这个确认，如何重塑目标函数？
q_en: How does confirming 'two-sided optimization' reshape the objective?
why: 双边市场要同时对买方（满意度/转化）和卖方（曝光公平、不赢家通吃）负责。这把单目标变成带公平约束的多目标：要么加公平性约束/正则，要么做约束优化，防止只优化买方点击而让长尾卖家被系统性埋没。单边优化没有这层。
why_en: A two-sided market must serve buyers (satisfaction) and sellers (fair exposure), turning a single objective into a fairness-constrained multi-objective problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果平台明确只对买方负责（如自营、无第三方卖家），单边优化买方满意度即可，不必引入卖方公平约束。
options: 只优化买方点击即可，卖方公平不影响系统设计
单目标变成带公平约束的多目标，防长尾卖家被埋没
双边优化就是把买卖两个模型的分数简单相加，无需约束
卖方公平只是运营政策，和模型的目标函数无关
options_en: Just optimize buyer clicks; seller fairness doesn't touch the system design.
It turns a single objective into a fairness-constrained multi-objective so long-tail sellers are not buried.
Two-sided optimization just sums the buyer and seller model scores, with no constraints.
Seller fairness is only an ops policy, unrelated to the model objective.
optionExplanations: 只优化买方点击会让长尾卖家被埋，长期损害供给侧，双边市场撑不住。
对；双边责任把问题变成带公平约束的多目标，约束防止赢家通吃。
简单相加不保证公平；需要显式约束/正则来平衡两侧。
公平在双边市场是要写进目标/约束的建模问题，不只是运营政策。
optionExplanations_en: Optimizing only buyer clicks buries long-tail sellers, hurting supply long-term and breaking the marketplace.
Correct — two-sided responsibility becomes a fairness-constrained multi-objective, with constraints preventing winner-take-all.
Simply adding models doesn't guarantee fairness; you need explicit constraints/regularization to balance both sides.
In a two-sided market, fairness is a modeling concern to encode in the objective/constraints, not just ops policy.
tradeoff: 买方转化 vs 卖方曝光公平：单目标最大化点击 vs 带公平约束的多目标（要牺牲一点买方指标）。

scenario: 澄清问题也能问砸：有些问法反而暴露你不成熟或浪费时间。
scenario_en: Clarifying can backfire: some question styles reveal immaturity or waste time.
q: 澄清阶段要避免哪些反模式？(多选)
q_en: Which anti-patterns should you avoid during clarification? (multiple)
why: 两大反模式：(1) 问没有设计影响的问题（如「后端用什么语言」）——不改变形式化，纯浪费时间；(2) 问太多、多到面试官要出手把你拉回正题。正解是问少而准的高影响问题，并把确认的答案可见地写下来当审计轨迹。
why_en: The two anti-patterns are asking questions with no design impact (like backend language) and asking so many that the interviewer must redirect you.
options: 问没有设计影响的问题，例如「后端用什么编程语言」
问到面试官不得不打断、把你拉回正题的程度
把每个确认的答案可见地写成编号需求清单
在面试官说「你定」时，明确陈述你的假设并写下来
options_en: Asking questions with no design impact, e.g. 'what backend language?'
Asking so many questions that the interviewer must interrupt and redirect you.
Writing every confirmed answer visibly as a numbered requirements list.
When the interviewer says 'up to you,' stating your assumption explicitly and writing it down.
optionExplanations: 对；无设计影响的问题（编程语言、云厂商）改变不了形式化，是纯浪费。
对；问题多到失控会让面试官出手拉你，暴露你不会控节奏。
错方向——这是好习惯：写下需求形成可见审计轨迹，不是反模式。
错方向——这是好习惯：面试官甩球时陈述并写下假设，展示资深的主人翁意识。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — no-design-impact questions (language, vendor) can't change the formulation and are pure waste.
Correct — asking so many that it spirals makes the interviewer redirect you, revealing poor pacing.
Wrong direction — this is a good habit: writing requirements as a visible audit trail is not an anti-pattern.
Wrong direction — this is a good habit: stating and recording an assumption when handed the ball shows senior judgment.

scenario: 你问了一个澄清问题，面试官耸耸肩说：「这个你来定(up to you)。」
scenario_en: You ask a clarifying question and the interviewer shrugs: 'up to you.'
q: 面试官把球踢回来说「你定」，最该怎么接？
q_en: When the interviewer says 'up to you,' what's the best response?
why: 别把「你定」当成没约束。明确陈述你的假设并写下来——「那我假设延迟预算是 200ms，基于首页实时场景」。这展示了对模糊性的资深主人翁意识：你不逃避不确定，而是负责任地定下一个可追溯的前提。
why_en: Don't treat 'up to you' as no constraint: state your assumption explicitly and write it down, so the ambiguity becomes a premise you can be held to.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个维度对设计确实无关紧要，可以简短带过不必长篇假设——但涉及关键约束时一定要显式定一个前提。
options: 既然对方说随便，就跳过延迟约束，直接画架构图
明确陈述假设并写下来，如「假设 200ms 预算」
反复追问延迟具体是 100ms 还是 200ms，逼对方给数字
心里默认延迟是 200ms，但不说出来也不写下来
options_en: Since they said whatever, skip the latency constraint and jump straight to the architecture diagram.
State the assumption explicitly and write it down, e.g. 'assume a 200ms budget'.
Keep pressing on whether it's 100ms or 200ms until the interviewer gives an exact number.
Silently default to 200ms latency in your head without saying or writing it down.
optionExplanations: 跳过延迟约束不代表它消失，后面的设计缺了这条前提照样会在容量估算处崩。
对；显式假设+写下来，把不确定变成可追溯前提，正是资深主人翁意识。
对方已让你定，再追问具体数字只会显得你不敢担责、浪费时间。
默认了 200ms 却不说出来，面试官看不到你的推理也无法追溯，等于白定。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the constraint doesn't make it disappear — the design breaks later at capacity estimation without it.
Correct — an explicit, written assumption turns uncertainty into a traceable premise you stand behind.
They already handed it to you; pressing for the exact number just wastes time and looks like you can't commit.
Defaulting to 200ms in your head without saying it hides your reasoning from the interviewer — untraceable.
tradeoff: 显式假设 vs 追问到底：自主推进 vs 等一个确定答案，前者要承担假设定错的风险。

scenario: 面试总长约 45 分钟，你想合理分配澄清和设计的时间。
scenario_en: The interview is about 45 minutes; you want to budget clarification versus design time.
q: 澄清阶段大约应占多长，剩下留给什么？
q_en: About how long should clarification take, and what gets the rest?
why: 目标是 5–8 分钟内达成需求清晰，把剩下 35+ 分钟留给架构、特征、模型、评估。这是节奏经验值：太短会漏约束、锚定；太长会挤掉设计时间、被面试官叫停。它是时间预算的分配基准。
why_en: Aim to reach clarity in 5-8 minutes so 35+ minutes remain for architecture, features, model, and evaluation — a pacing rule of thumb, not a formula.
options: 澄清占 20 分钟，越充分越好，设计部分随便压一压
约 5–8 分钟收敛需求，剩下 35+ 分钟给设计
澄清 1 分钟就够，绝大部分时间用来写代码和调参
整场都在澄清，把设计留到面试结束后再补交给面试官
options_en: Spend 20 minutes clarifying — the more the better — and squeeze the design.
About 5-8 minutes to converge requirements, leaving 35+ minutes for the design.
One minute of clarification is enough; spend the rest writing code and tuning.
Clarify the whole time and send the design to the interviewer afterwards.
optionExplanations: 澄清占 20 分钟会挤掉设计与深挖，多半被面试官叫停。
对；5–8 分钟收敛需求、留 35+ 分钟做实质设计，是被推荐的时间分配。
1 分钟框不清问题，容易锚定、漏关键约束。
全程澄清不产出设计，等于没完成面试的主体任务。
optionExplanations_en: 20 minutes of clarification crowds out design and deep dives and usually gets stopped.
Correct — 5-8 minutes to converge needs, leaving 35+ for substantive design, is the recommended split.
One minute can't frame the problem and invites anchoring and missed constraints.
Clarifying the whole time produces no design and misses the interview's main task.

scenario: 十领域问题库的用法：不是背全，而是每个领域记住少数几个最能改写设计的高命中问题。
scenario_en: How to use the ten-domain bank: not memorize all, but keep a few high-hit questions per domain that most reshape the design.
q: 补全领域问题库的使用法则：
q_en: Fill in the rule for using the domain question bank:
text: 每个领域记住 {{2–3}} 个问题以防临场卡壳(freezing)，并优先问那些 {{最能改写设计}} 的问题，而不是把所有问题背全。
text_en: Memorize {{2-3}} questions per domain to avoid freezing, and prioritize the ones that {{most affect the design}} rather than reciting them all.
why: 问题库不是背诵清单，而是防卡壳的锚点：每领域记住 2–3 个高命中问题，紧张时也能张口；再从中挑最能改写设计的先问。贪多反而变成没有设计影响的乱问。
why_en: The bank is an anti-freeze anchor: keep 2-3 high-hit questions per domain so you can start even when nervous, and ask the design-changing ones first.

scenario: 有人觉得五个镜头顺序无所谓，反正都会问到。你要解释为什么规模约束要早问。
scenario_en: Someone thinks the five lenses' order doesn't matter since you'll ask all of them. Explain why scale/constraints go early.
q: 为什么把「规模与约束」放在靠前问，而不是最后？
q_en: Why ask 'scale and constraints' early rather than last?
why: 早问规模约束能尽快剪掉不可行的架构：知道是 10M 请求/秒还是 10K 请求/天，你才不会在一个单次重打分方案上白花时间才发现它扛不住。约束前置=尽早收敛可行空间，避免在无效方案上投入。
why_en: Asking scale early prunes infeasible architectures fast, so you don't invest in a design that can't hold the load before finding out.
options: 顺序无所谓，规模留到最后再问也完全一样
早问规模能尽快剪掉扛不住负载的架构，少走弯路
规模要最后问，因为它只影响上线后的扩容计划
规模只对面试官重要，对候选人的设计推导没用
options_en: Order doesn't matter; asking about scale last works exactly the same.
Asking scale early prunes architectures that cannot hold the load, avoiding detours.
Ask scale last, since it only affects the post-launch capacity plan.
Scale only matters to the interviewer, not to the candidate reasoning.
optionExplanations: 顺序有讲究：约束晚问，你可能已经在不可行方案上花了大量时间。
对；规模前置让你尽早排除装不下负载的架构，把精力留给可行方案。
规模不止影响扩容，它先决定架构形态（单次 vs 多阶段）。
规模恰恰决定候选人该选哪类架构，对设计至关重要。
optionExplanations_en: Order matters: asking constraints late risks having already invested in an infeasible design.
Correct — asking scale early rules out architectures that can't hold the load, saving effort for feasible ones.
Scale isn't just capacity planning; it first decides the architecture shape (single-pass vs multi-stage).
Scale is exactly what decides which architecture class the candidate should pick — crucial to the design.
